label: Brand gallery
title: A tilted wordmark, a lot of green, and a voucher
lede: Groupon’s brand was a wordmark and a tone of voice: deal descriptions written as jokes. Here are the marks as the archive kept them, two photographs under free licenses, and our own drawings.

archive.caption: The early logo with its tagline, “Collective Buying Power.”
archive.alt: Groupon wordmark on a dark tilted panel with the words Collective Buying Power
archive.credit: Cropped from an Internet Archive capture of groupon.com. Shown for commentary; trademarks belong to their owners.

archive.caption: The logo at the time of the Google talks and the IPO.
archive.alt: Groupon wordmark in white on a dark tilted panel
archive.credit: Cropped from an Internet Archive capture of groupon.com. Shown for commentary; trademarks belong to their owners.

archive.caption: The Point, the site Groupon grew out of. The capture is unstyled.
archive.alt: Unstyled archived page headed The Point: People Solving Problems
archive.credit: Internet Archive capture of thepoint.com. Shown for commentary.

archive.caption: Andrew Mason, founder and chief executive until February 2013, at the e-G8 Forum in Paris.
archive.alt: Andrew Mason speaking on stage, seated, in a dark jacket
archive.credit: Photo: Aaron Fulkerson, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Andrew_Mason_(cropped).jpg), CC BY-SA 2.0. Resized.

archive.caption: A Groupon parade float photographed on June 29, 2014, with the slogan “Check Groupon first.” The photograph’s description does not name the event.
archive.alt: Parade float with a large sign reading Check Groupon First and people in green shirts
archive.credit: Photo: nathanmac87, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Groupon_Float_(14537747014).jpg), CC BY 2.0. Resized.
